sources.entry: Video surveillance, also known as Closed-circuit television (CCTV), is the use of video cameras for surveillance in areas that require additional security or ongoing monitoring.

summary.name: Closed-circuit television

summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines CCTV as cameras transmitting video to a limited set of monitors rather than open broadcast, and traces its history from a 1927 mechanical system and 1949 Vericon commercial system through reel-to-reel tape, VCR, digital multiplexing, and internet and mobile viewing. It covers uses such as crime prevention, traffic monitoring, forensics, schools, homes, and workplaces, and summarizes mixed research on crime reduction. It also reports prevalence figures for Asia, the Americas, Russia, and Europe, along with privacy concerns.
notable: Covers CCTV history from 1927 to the internet and mobile era
Summarizes mixed research on CCTV effectiveness in reducing crime
Reports country-level camera counts and privacy debates
caveats: Describes a general technology topic, not a downloadable product or software
Crime-reduction evidence is mixed and some studies are methodologically questioned
Camera counts vary significantly between sources
